Remove a test from the mprotect() path which checks that the mprotect()ed
range on a hugepage VMA is hugepage aligned (yes
is_aligned_hugepage_range() is the opposite of what you'd guess :-/).

column2: we don't need this test.  If the given addresses match the

column1: beginning/end of a hugepage VMA they must already be suitably aligned.  If

column2: then mprotect_fixup() will attempt to split the VMA.  The very

column1: first test in split_vma() will check for a badly aligned address on a
hugepage VMA and return -EINVAL if necessary.
identify of hugetlb pte is lost when changing page protection via mprotect.
A page fault occurs later will trigger a bug check in huge_pte_alloc().
The fix is to always make new pte a hugetlb pte and also to clean up
legacy code where _PAGE_PRESENT is forced on in the pre-faulting day.
